item.title: Thursday, August 27th, 2026
item.description:
# During the period of peak leaks about the Pixel 11 series, I was all set on upgrading to the Pixel 11 Pro XL from my current 10 Pro XL. The promise of camera enhancements and the Tensor G6 chip being built on a 2nm process looked like it would a be decent upgrade.

It transpired that the 2nm rumours were wrong and the camera upgrades weren't as good as anticipated. Combined with the price increases and drop in base RAM, I decided to stick with what I've got.

While there are some nice features on the 11 series, knowing how I use my phone, I'm not sure I will really miss out. When you also consider that many software features eventually find their way to older devices, it might just be a case of wait and see.

The upgrade deal with my carrier means my current phone would have been traded in and refurbished, so it would not have become e-waste, but I still think this is the right decision.

It's no secret that I view phone cases as a necessary evil and am constantly looking for the thinnest, least intrusive case I can find. I went with a full body skin for a while but had problems with the side pieces coming off. I replaced the back skin and returned to a clear case as a compromise.

I've had my eye on something else for a while: a metal 'bumper style' frame that clips around the phone with a separate portion that sticks over the camera bar. While it is just a frame and doesn't have a back, the skin keeps the rest of th phone protected from scratches.

The frame is a little thicker than I expected but doesn't add anything to the depth of the phone beyond a (very) small lip which keeps the screen off a flat surface if placed face down.

I really like it.

item.title: Saturday, August 22nd, 2026
item.description:
# At some point during the site tweaks, I managed to create a regression with /reader. I don't know how or when, but things just stopped working properly and only a few feeds would update. I'm not even sure that I made database specific changes around the time things stopped working. 🤷‍♂️

I initially thought it might be a specific feed causing a problem so backed up my OPML and started deleting them one-by-one.

No dice.

I ended up doing a full refactor before re-adding all the feeds. I still don't know exactly what happened, but at least it's working.

item.title: Thursday, August 20th, 2026
item.description:
# Thursday last week saw me back at the doctor's for a two month review of the fluoxetine. While it's certainly better than the citalopram (not hard) I don't think it's fully there yet.

My wife says my mood swings have been less frequent but more noticeable, wider. I'm not sure if they appear that way because there is a bigger gap or whether there is actually a bigger swing. Could the size be inversely proportional to frequency? 1

My dosage has been doubled and I've got to keep a "mood diary" to see if I settle or if the swings get even wider on a higher dose.

Now that I've been on this for a week I think I'm a bit more stable, but I'll really need to check in with my wife as she is the one who really notices. I often find it hard to judge how I am; what I often consider feeling flat is actually a low but it doesn't seem to register that way with me.

  1. Apparently there's no direct correlation between duration and severity ↩

item.title: Wednesday, August 19th, 2026
item.description:
# New EP dropping on Friday.
That's right, my next release is just a couple of days away. It is called "is, was, and always will be" including 6 acid tracks across different styles.

It will initially be available from Subvert.fm for a two week exclusive period, followed by the usual release on Bandcamp and a listening party.

I have uploaded the video for "104 and change" to YouTube as a preview.

item.title: Tuesday, August 11th, 2026
item.description:
# I looked down at my watch earlier to see a crack right across the glass 😱

I don't even remember bashing it at any point this morning.

Luckily, on inspection, it was the protector I'd put on and not the watch itself. 😅 I was worried as I couldn't feel the crack at all.

At least the protector did its job.
